resources.string: Enable support for different insulin concentrations (U50, U200, etc.)

Enable bolus advisor which assists with bolus calculations during higher glycemias.
Enable bolus reminder notifications to help track insulin administration.

Switches off the phone\'s bluetooth for one second if no connection to the pump is possible. This may help on some phones where the bluetooth stack freezes.
Alert if no BG data is received
Raise urgent alarms as Android notifications
On: alarms ring even when the phone is silent or in Do Not Disturb. Off: alarms do not ring then. In Do Not Disturb they only vibrate.
Create sensor change therapy event when sensor is inserted.
Use DynamicISF for sensitivity adjustment instead of Autosens.
Enable Super Micro Bolus. SMB delivers insulin immediately to respond to rising blood glucose.
Enable SMB with high temp target
Allow SMB when high temporary target is active.
Enable SMB in all conditions regardless of bolus or COB.

Allow SMB for a period after carbs are entered.
Enable Unannounced Meals detection and treatment.
When sensitivity is detected, raise the target glucose.

Always use short average delta instead of simple delta for BG change calculations.
Adjust sensitivity calculations when using DynamicISF.

resources.string: Send notifications to watch when SMB is delivered.
Broadcast AAPS data to 3rd party watch apps via intent.
Number of carbs to add when button is pressed
Apply this value to BG and carbs correction in bolus wizard\'s result
Deliver full bolus (100%) if glycemia is older than
App launch and when returning to the app. Independent from other levels
Open Loop will popup new change request only if change is bigger than this value in %. Default value is 20%
Max minutes of basal to limit SMB
UAM max minutes of basal to limit SMB
Minimum grams of carbs to display a carbs suggestion alert. Carbs suggestions below this number will not trigger a notification.
Set to a number, e.g. 160, which means when temp target is 160 mg/dL and High temptarget raises sensitivity=true, run 50%% basal at this level (120 = 75%%; 140 = 60%%).
Percentage of maxIOB above which SMBs are disabled.\nDefault value: 100%\nWith 100% this feature is effectively disabled.
Adjustment factor for DynamicISF. Set more than 100% for more aggressive correction doses, and less than 100% for less aggressive corrections.
Amount of hours in the past for sensitivity detection (carbs absorption time is excluded)
Default number of days of data to be processed by Autotune (up to 30)
Add noise, jitter timestamps, randomize trend arrows, and emit occasional random carbs. Disable for a clean deterministic sine wave with the trend arrow derived from the sine slope.
Name of the person using this phone. It tells this AAPS instance apart in reports and sync.
Choose dark, light, or to follow the system theme
Additional mandatory PIN at token end
Additional digits that should be memorised and glued at end of each generated One Time Password
Enter your Nightscout API secret (min. 12 characters)
Enter your Nightscout access token (min. 17 characters)
Amount of insulin to add when button is pressed
This value is called max basal in OpenAPS context
This value is called Max IOB in OpenAPS context\nOpenAPS will not add more insulin if current IOB is greater than this value. Value is affected by patient type too.
This value is called Max IOB in OpenAPS context\nThis is maximal insulin in [U] APS can deliver at once. Value is affected by patient type too.

Default value: 3 This is a key OpenAPS safety cap. What this does is limit your basals to be 3x (in this people) your biggest basal rate. You likely will not need to change this, but you should be aware that’s what is discussed about “3x max daily; 4x current” for safety caps.

Default value: 4 This is the other half of the key OpenAPS safety caps, and the other half of “3x max daily; 4x current” of the safety caps. This means your basal, regardless of max basal set on your pump, cannot be any higher than this number times the current level of your basal. This is to prevent people from getting into dangerous territory by setting excessively high max basals before understanding how the algorithm works. Again, the default is 4x; most people will never need to adjust this and are instead more likely to need to adjust other settings if they feel like they are “running into” this safety cap.

Default value: 2\nBolus snooze is enacted after you do a meal bolus, so the loop won’t counteract with low temps when you’ve just eaten. The example here and default is 2; so a 3 hour DIA means that bolus snooze will be gradually phased out over 1.5 hours (3DIA/2).

Default value: 3.0 (AMA) or 8.0 (SMB). This is a setting for default carb absorption impact per 5 minutes. The default is an expected 3mg/dl/5min. This affects how fast COB are decayed, and how much carb absorption is assumed in calculating future predicted BG, when BG is falling more than expected, or not rising as much as expected.
Time at which any meal is considered absorbed. Remaining carbs will be cut off.
Time in hours where is expected all carbs from meal will be absorbed
Default value: 0.7\nThe other side of the autosens safety limits, putting a cap on how low autosens can adjust basals, and how high it can adjust ISF and BG targets.

Default value: 1.2\nThis is a multiplier cap for autosens (and soon autotune) to set a 20%% max limit on how high the autosens ratio can be, which in turn determines how high autosens can adjust basals, how low it can adjust ISF, and how low it can set the BG target.
Similar to autosens_min this defines how weak ISF can become.\n\nThe default value 1.0 effectively shuts off this effect.

Similar to autosens_max this defines how strong ISF can become.

The default value 1.0 effectively shuts off this effect.

WARNING: Be extremely careful when using values above 2.5
This is the weight applied while glucose accelerates and which strengthens ISF thereby potentially increasing insulin delivery.\n\nThe default value 0.0 effectively shuts off this effect.
This is the weight applied while glucose decelerates and which weakens ISF thereby potentially reducing insulin delivery.\n\nThe default value 0.0 effectively shuts off this effect.
This is the weight applied while glucose is below target and which weakens ISF thereby potentially reducing insulin delivery.\n\nThe default value 0.0 effectively shuts off this effect.
This is the weight applied while glucose is above target and which strengthens ISF thereby potentially increasing insulin delivery.\n\nThe default value 0.0 effectively shuts off this effect.

Default value: 0. The linearly increasing SMB delivery ratio is mapped to the glucose range [target_bg, target_bg+bg_range].\nAt target_bg the SMB ratio is smb_delivery_ratio_min, at target_bg+bg_range it is smb_delivery_ratio_max\nWith 0 the linearly increasing SMB ratio is disabled and the fixed smb_delivery_ratio is used.
This is the weight applied while glucose is rising and which strengthens ISF thereby potentially increasing insulin delivery.\n\nThe default value 0.0 effectively shuts off this effect.

This is the weight applied during longer lasting, elevated glucose plateaus and which strengthens ISF thereby potentially increasing insulin delivery.\n\nThe default value 0.0 effectively shuts off this effect.

Default value: 0.5 This is another key OpenAPS safety cap, and specifies what share of the total insulin required can be delivered as SMB. This is to prevent people from getting into dangerous territory by setting SMB requests from the caregivers phone at the same time. Increase this experimental value slowly and with caution.
Default value: 0.5 This is the lower end of a linearly increasing ratio rather than the fix value above.
Default value: 0.5 This is the upper end of a linearly increasing ratio rather than the fix value above.
Default value: 1 This is another key OpenAPS safety cap, and specifies by what factor you can exceed the regular 120 maxSMB/maxUAM minutes. Increase this experimental value slowly and with caution.

BG value below which insulin is suspended. Default value uses standard target model. User can set value between 60mg/dl (3.3mmol/l) and 100mg/dl(5.5mmol/l). Values below 65/3.6 result in use of default model

Run the loop on every sensor reading rather than once per five minutes. No effect on a five-minute sensor. On a one-minute sensor this makes the loop run every minute, which also allows more frequent SMBs.
Allow Boost with High Temp Targets
Use traditional Autosens when TDD is off
Disable Night Mode with low temp target
Percentage of algorithm-determined insulin to deliver as SMB. Default: 50
Maximum individual bolus from Boost. Default: 2.5 U
Multiplier for calculated Boost insulin. Values >=3 disable Boost. Default: 1.0
Maximum IOB for accelerated bolusing. Above this, regular oref1 used. Default: 1.0 U
Applies time-of-day ISF adjustment based on circadian rhythm model
Allow Boost when high temp target is active (exercise)
Calculate ISF from Total Daily Dose using the logarithmic formula. When disabled, uses profile ISF directly

Adjust sensitivity ratio using 24h TDD / 7D TDD, similar to Autosens. Needs TDD-based ISF, and is switched off automatically when TDD-based ISF is off and when Boost is first enabled. Recommended to start with this off

When TDD-based ISF is off, let Autosens adjust basal, target and CR. Requires Autosens enabled. When this is off as well, no sensitivity adjustment is applied. No effect when TDD-based ISF is on, since TDD owns sensitivity then.
Reference BG target for ISF calculation. Default: 99

Controls how much your current blood glucose level affects ISF. At 100%, ISF is fully adjusted by BG (higher BG = stronger ISF). At 50%, only half the BG-driven adjustment is applied. At 0%, BG has no effect and ISF stays at the target-level value regardless of current BG. Needs TDD-based ISF: set to 0 automatically when TDD-based ISF is switched off, and to 100 when it is switched on. Default: 100
BG above this value is softened to reduce ISF aggressiveness at very high BG. Default: 210
Scale the calculated TDD by this percentage. Default: 100
Steps/hour below which user is inactive. Default: 500
Hours after Boost start to allow sleep-in. Default: 2
Steps/hour below which user is considered still sleeping. Default: 250
Steps in 5 min above which user is active. Default: 420
Steps in 15 min above which user is active. Default: 800
Steps in 30 min above which user is active. Default: 1200
Steps in 60 min above which user is active. Default: 1800

Use heart rate data to classify exercise type (aerobic vs resistance) and confirm step-count signals. Requires a wearable sending HR data to AAPS. Feature is opt-in and falls back to step-only detection if no recent HR data is available.
Your maximum heart rate in BPM used for Karvonen zone calculation. Standard estimate: 220 minus age. Default 180 bpm is conservative for adults when age is unknown. Range 150–220.
Your resting heart rate in BPM used for Karvonen Heart Rate Reserve method. Measure on waking before getting up. Default 60 bpm. Range 30–100.
How many minutes of recent HR data to average for exercise classification. Default 15 min gives a stable reading. Range 5–60 min.

Detect elevated HR without movement as possible stress or illness. Reduces insulin aggressiveness (raises target) when HR is in zone 2+ but steps are very low. Separate opt-in; disable if you experience false positives.
Automatically set a high TempTarget and reduce SMB aggressiveness after exercise to guard against delayed hypoglycemia
How long the recovery TempTarget and SMB reduction remain active after exercise ends. Evidence supports 1–4h; default 2h covers the primary risk window (Riddell et al.)
BG target during recovery window. ATTD 2020 consensus recommends 7–10 mmol/L (126–180 mg/dL) after aerobic exercise; default 8.0 mmol/L / 144 mg/dL
Multiplier (0.0–1.0) applied to boost_bolus and boost_scale during the recovery window. 0.5 = 50% reduction. Applies even if TempTarget is cancelled manually.
Recovery only triggers if exercise was detected for at least this many minutes. Avoids false triggers from brief activity bursts. Default: 10 min.
Disable SMBs during night hours when BG is near target
Start of Night Mode window (24h format HH:mm). Default: 22:00
End of Night Mode window (24h format HH:mm). Default: 07:00
SMBs are disabled when BG is below the profile target plus this offset. Default: 1.5 mmol/L (27 mg/dL)
Allow SMBs during Night Mode if carbs are on board
Allow SMBs during Night Mode when temp target is below profile target

When ON, sleep state (heart rate + steps) drives Night Mode in addition to the time window. Engages early (PRE_SLEEP) ApsBoostPreSleepLeadMin before nightStart to limit IOB before bed; stays active past nightEnd if still sleeping. Wake requires BOTH HR rise and step activity (BG trend alone does not wake). Requires a HR source (Wear OS / Garmin).
How many minutes before Night Mode Start to enter PRE_SLEEP and engage Night Mode SMB suppression. Default 60.
HR + steps conditions must hold for this many minutes before SLEEPING is confirmed. Default 10.
HR > 1.25× resting AND steps ≥ 100 must both hold for this many minutes before exiting SLEEPING. Default 5.

Reads heart rate from Android Health Connect on a polling cadence. Lets Garmin Connect / Wear OS HR flow into Boost continuously (including overnight) without needing the watch field to be actively pulling glucose. Requires the user to install Health Connect (on Android < 14) and grant Read Heart Rate permission. Open Health Connect settings to grant.
How often to query Health Connect for new HR records. Lower = fresher data, slightly more battery. Default 5.

Logging only: never changes dosing. Reads daily steps from Health Connect (single source, de-duplicated), learns your personal step baseline, and logs to Nightscout what an activity/inactivity sensitivity modifier WOULD do (e.g. \"wouldΔISF +12%\" after a high-activity day). Needs Health Connect Read Steps permission granted. For data-gathering ahead of a future feature.

Total SMB insulin (U) that may be delivered in any rolling 60-minute window. Caps insulin stacking during sustained climbs. Set to 0 to disable. Factory default: 10 U (non-binding); auto-configuration tightens it to your own history (Confirmed cap + 2× Committed cap).

Within-user trial. On randomised treatment days the post-rescue rebound guard is capped at 60% and applies across the whole window instead of switching off above 170 mg/dL. Neither arm can deliver more insulin than the current behaviour. Leave OFF unless you are enrolled.
Scales the catch-up dose at meal CONFIRMED. 1.0 = calibrated default; lower = gentler commit dose, higher = more aggressive. Range 0.7-1.3.
Multiplier on the ML hypo-risk damper floor. 1.0 = default; raise toward 2.0 for hypo unawareness or after a recent severe hypo. Range 1.0-2.0.
Scales the per-cycle insulin (aggression) budget. 1.0 = default; below 1.0 for sensitive users, above for resistant. Range 0.8–1.2.
Hard upper limit on the confirmed meal SMB. Default: 2.5 U
Hard upper limit on the per-cycle committed meal SMB. Default: 0.5 U

When a rise is sharp AND accelerating AND the meal score corroborates (and you\'re awake, not exercising), Boost confirms the meal in one cycle instead of waiting — so fast carbs get covered ~15 min earlier. Replay-validated to avoid firing on sleep/compression. Toggle off to revert to the standard observe-confirm timing.

Confirms a meal one cycle sooner still when its signal is confirm-strength on two consecutive cycles — the same shot, delivered a touch earlier. Because it occasionally commits to a rise that would have faded, it adds a little insulin, so it is set automatically only for users whose recent low-glucose exposure is well within target. Default OFF; auto-config turns it on where it is safe. Leave off (or turn off) to keep the standard confirm timing.

Enforces a 25% floor on the composed soft-brake multiplier during active meal sessions above 160 mg/dL with eventualBG above target — fixes the soft-brake stack compounding to sub-pump-step zero doses mid-meal (July 2026). All hard gates and dose caps still apply. Default OFF. ENFORCED hypo-gate: the floor engages ONLY while BOTH your trailing 14-day time below 63 mg/dL (3.5 mmol/L) is under 2.0% AND your time below 70 mg/dL is under 3.5% — it is insulin-adding, so it stays suppressed (even when this is ON) if either low-exposure figure is higher, and auto-re-engages when both drop back under their limits.

When you are above 180 mg/dL but oref calculates no extra insulin is needed (it predicts you will come down on the insulin already on board), this delivers a small hold — up to 0.5 U, capped at your committed-cap and your IOB headroom — to bring highs down a little faster. It deliberately doses a touch more than the base algorithm on that high tail, so it is for users who prefer a firmer response to sustained highs. Excludes decelerating highs, sleep, and the post-rescue window; all hard hypo gates still apply. Default OFF. Uses the SAME ENFORCED hypo-gate as the brake floor: engages ONLY while your trailing 14-day time below 63 mg/dL is under 2.0% AND time below 70 mg/dL is under 3.5%, and auto-suspends if either rises.

Fizzle-safe early primer delivered on an accelerating rise during OBSERVING — gives an earlier meal response. Additive up to this base; any velocity-scaled excess is netted off the CONFIRMED commit-shot (move, not add). 0 = OFF. Auto-config derives a per-user value.

Override: deliver the acceleration primer as a bolus even if auto-config routed you to the retractable temp-basal fallback (for hypo-prone users). Floors and the commit-shot net-off are unaffected. Default OFF (respect auto-config routing).

Experimental, off by default. Splits the confirm commitment, giving part at the confirming cycle and holding the rest for ten minutes, released only if the rise continues. Can only deliver less insulin than without it, never more. A held remainder that cannot be delivered, because the rolling cumulative cap is spent or the sleep gate is shut, counts as a decision not to release.
Share of the sized confirm dose delivered at the confirming cycle. The remainder is held. Set to 1.0 to make the tranche inert without switching it off.

The remainder is released when the rule\'s probability exceeds this. Higher withholds more. Auto-config sets it from your own confirm episodes over the last 45 days once there are at least 15 that clearly went big or stayed small, with at least 5 of each. It raises it whenever your episodes support that and does not currently lower it. A value you set here yourself is kept; set it back to 0.48 to hand it back to auto-config.

Experimental: learns your habitual meal times (from Boost meal commits) and applies a low target shortly before a learned meal so insulin is working when carbs land. Exercise and post-exercise recovery override it. When OFF it only logs (\"V6 pre-meal WOULD apply\" without changing dosing) so you can verify the learned times first.
The low target applied during the pre-meal window. Lower = more pre-emptive insulin. Default: 72 mg/dL (4.0 mmol).
How many minutes before a learned meal the low target window OPENS. It closes 45 min before the meal. Default: 60 min.
